item.text: I’ll audit the package on its own stated interface, treating OL-1/2/3 as permitted assumptions and looking specifically for undeclared dependencies or ill-defined carrier clauses.

## (a) Carrier design

> “ν_i = (e_i, h_i, ℓ_i, s_i, u_i, sel_i, inc_i)”

> “Equality on 𝔈 := literal componentwise equality (all constituents live in explicitly constructed countable sets…)”

**Critical error.** No domains are declared for \(s_i\) and \(u_i\). Consequently the set \(\mathfrak E\), and hence its claimed componentwise equality, is not fully defined. This reproduces the architectural class of defect the carrier design was supposed to eliminate.

> “for i ≥ 1, Lift_i(c) := … an ARBITRARY BUT FIXED function of c”

> “𝔗 consists of the GMN type chains … in which every representative is the Lift of its own chain datum”

> “The family F_rep := image of Lift has, by construction, the exact shape of (L5)’s Convention”

**Critical error.** An arbitrary monic polynomial of the prescribed degree need not be a GMN representative. Thus its image does not “by construction” have the shape required by (L5). This becomes true only under OL-1. Before OL-1, \(\Theta(\mathbf H)\) need not belong to the declared codomain \(\mathfrak T\), so the advertised global map \(\Theta:\mathfrak E\to\mathfrak T\) is not unconditionally defined.

The literal equality on \(\mathfrak T\) itself is coherent once admissibility is assumed: the datum and its representative are uniquely tied by the fixed function, and no quotient by representative equivalence is used.

> “only the last node may be terminal”

> “For 𝐇 with continuing nodes ν₁, …, ν_{k′}: Θ(𝐇) := the chain…”

**Critical error.** A terminal last node is part of equality on \(\mathfrak E\), but is completely discarded by \(\Theta\). This is not merely harmless noninjectivity of the unrestricted carrier: it directly contradicts the later recovery claims under `Cons_f`, because `Cons_f` likewise imposes no conditions on terminal-node fields.

The W-laws themselves are internally compatible. In particular, T4 forces \(g_i=\mu_i=1\) through \(\mu_i g_i\leq\ell_i=1\), and W3 therefore prevents a T4 node from being interior. Same-degree steps \(e_i=f_i=1\) are not forbidden by the stated version of (L1).

## (b) Order \(\leq1\)

> “Let … 𝐇 = (ρ₀) or (ρ₀; ν₁) … Then … (D1) … \(f_1=g_1\), … \(m_2=e_1(f_0g_1)\) … \(v_2(\phi_1)=h_1\) … \(\deg G=m_2\mu_1\)”

**Critical error.** For \(\mathbf H=(\rho_0)\), and also for a one-node history whose node is terminal, \(e_1,h_1,g_1,\mu_1,\psi_1\), and \(G\) are not defined. The theorem is therefore not even a well-formed statement for part of its explicitly quantified domain.

> “(D0) … 𝐇 is recoverable from \((f,\Theta(\mathbf H))\) — i.e. Θ is injective on \(\{\mathrm{Cons}_f=\mathrm{true},\text{ length}\leq1\}\)”

> “from Θ(𝐇) read off \((\widehat\psi_0,e_1,h_1,\widehat\psi_1)\)…”

**Critical error.** The proof silently assumes that \(\nu_1\) is continuing. If \(\nu_1\) is terminal, \(\Theta(\rho_0;\nu_1)=\Theta(\rho_0)\), while `Cons_f` checks only (c0). Distinct terminal records therefore have identical images and can all be consistent with the same \(f\). The claimed injectivity and recovery are false.

> “(D0) Θ is total and truncation-compatible on 𝔈”

**Critical error.** Read literally, this asserts totality on all of \(\mathfrak E\), including orders at which an arbitrary `Lift_i` may not be a representative. OL-1 is unavailable in Theorem 1. The proof’s assertion that totality is “structural” does not establish codomain membership.

> “the principal part on abscissas \([0,\omega]\)”

**Justification gap.** If an initial \(\phi_1\)-adic coefficient vanishes—for example when \(\phi_1\) divides \(f\) exactly—the finite principal polygon need not occupy the entire interval from abscissa \(0\). The package itself acknowledges slope-\(-\infty\) contributions in (L8), but (D3) does not discuss this case. Assuming the intended restriction to a selected finite side, the subsequent finite-side formulas can continue.

Conditional on a continuing first node and a finite selected side, the core order-1 calculations are otherwise supported by the stated L1–L9 material:

- \(\deg G=m_1e_1\mu_1f_1=m_2\mu_1\) follows from (L6).
- \(v_2(\phi_1)=h_1\) follows from the stated Prop. 2.7 identity and \(v_1(\phi_1)=0\).
- W3 supplies precisely the non-completeness needed for Def. 3.10.
- Both lattice witnesses satisfy the stated region inequalities.
- The charge uses only nonnegative index summands and (L9).

Those valid calculations do not rescue the theorem as quantified.

## (c) Orders \(\geq2\) and the open lemmas

> “the stage window polygon … written in integer slot coordinates (denominators cleared)”

> “equals \(N_{i+1}^{-}(f)\) … up to the recorded translation”

**Justification gap.** Neither the coordinate-clearing map nor the “recorded translation” is defined. OL-2 consequently lacks an exact equality of coordinate systems. In particular, it does not precisely state how an initial point in the stage frame determines the GMN-frame pair \((s_i,u_i)\).

> “a stage residual computed from digit data and normalized by a distinguished ‘anchor’ unit”

> “the anchor-normalized stage residual … equals \(R_{\lambda_{i+1}}(f)\)”

**Justification gap.** “Digit data,” “anchor unit,” and the normalization operation are not defined. OL-3 states the desired conclusion, but not a proposition that can be independently attacked from the supplied interface.

> “𝐇 is recoverable from \((f,\Theta(\mathbf H))\) given the frame tie … via OL-2 at orders ≥ 2”

**Critical error.** OL-2 supplies side correspondence only “up to” an undefined translation and does not explicitly state recoverability of \((s_i,u_i)\). The higher-order injectivity proof consumes a stronger positional identification than OL-2 precisely states. Terminal-node nonrecoverability independently makes this claim false at every order.

> “Every history emitted by the stage flow on \(f\) … is … a \(\mathrm{Cons}_f\) history”

> “The W2/W3 laws are laws OF THE CARRIER; whether a concrete engine’s records satisfy them is out of scope here.”

**Critical error.** OL-1/2/3 establish representative admissibility, polygon correspondence, and residual correspondence. They do not establish W1–W5, especially W2, W3, or the rule that only the last node may be terminal. Section 4’s stage-flow interface does not impose those laws either. Theorem 2(D) therefore contains an undeclared dependence on an emission-discipline lemma, directly contrary to the scope remark.

> “Saturation at the last read … \(\mu_{k'}\) …”

**Critical error.** Theorem 2 allows \(k'=0\), but then \(\mu_{k'}\) and “the last read” are undefined. This repeats the zero-continuing-node defect in Theorem 1.

Assuming genuine continuing nodes, OL-1, and `Cons_f`, the type-tree induction, degree recursion, saturation argument, and per-order index charge are complete from the stated GMN facts. In particular, nothing from OL-2 or OL-3 is needed for the abstract `Cons_f`-conditional order-1 charge. But Theorem 2(D), higher-order positional recovery, and the global carrier map require additional undeclared content.

**VERDICT: UNSOUND**
